purpose: Primary evidence for the hardware gate's native-execution claim: which SASS architectures the shipped torch wheel actually contains, and that it contains NO PTX. Recorded because torch.cuda.get_arch_list() reports the BUILD CONFIGURATION string, not the fatbinary contents.

interpretation.B200_sm_100_CC_10_0: NATIVE AND DIRECT: 448 plain sm_100 cubins plus 59 sm_100a arch-specific kernels are compiled for exactly this architecture. No compatibility rule is relied upon.
interpretation.B300_sm_103_CC_10_3: NATIVE: the 448 plain sm_100 cubins execute on sm_103 under NVIDIA's same-major/higher-minor cubin compatibility rule (a cubin for X.y runs on X.z, z >= y), and the wheel additionally carries 59 sm_103a arch-tuned kernels matching the sm_100a count, i.e. PyTorch ships the arch-specific variants for both datacenter Blackwell targets.
interpretation.no_ptx: Zero PTX entries means JIT/PTX fallback is STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: a kernel either loads as native SASS or fails loudly. This is what makes the hardware gate's failure mode loud rather than silently-slow-or-wrong, and it is asserted at runtime by deploy/hardware_gate.py (any compute_* entry in the arch list refuses the machine).
interpretation.sm_100a_on_sm_103: The 'a' suffix means arch-specific and NOT forward compatible, so sm_100a kernels do not run on sm_103 — which is precisely why the equal count of sm_103a kernels matters, and why the gate additionally exercises real workload paths (BF16 GEMM, Ouro-RLTT forward/generation, backward+optimizer, intervention hook, checkpoint round-trip) before any scientific execution.

reproduce: cuobjdump --list-elf <venv>/lib/python3.14/site-packages/torch/lib/libtorch_cuda.so | grep -oE 'sm_[0-9]+[af]?' | sort | uniq -c; cuobjdump --list-ptx <same> | grep -c compute_
hardware_validation_status: NOT STARTED — this is static wheel evidence only; neither B300 nor B200 hardware has executed anything from this stack.
